notes: HSP 4 is a cardioid, pre-polarised condenser headworn microphone (headmic), not a device with a chassis full of labeled jacks — its only physical I/O is the terminating connector on its permanently-attached 1.6 m cable, which plugs into a Sennheiser wireless bodypack transmitter (or wired mixer input) to supply bias power (4.5–15 V) and carry the mic signal on the same connector; there is no separate power inlet. Sennheiser sells the HSP 4 in multiple cable-end variants for different transmitter families: the base "-3" SKU (used here) terminates in Sennheiser's proprietary 3-pin locking connector (for 2000/3000/5000-series and evolution wireless bodypacks); an "-EW" variant instead terminates in a locking 3.5 mm mini-jack; a "-5" variant ships with bare/tinned lead ends and no connector at all. None of the allowed connector ids exactly matches Sennheiser's proprietary 3-pin locking connector, so "xlr3" was chosen as the closest available id (3-pin locking analog mic connector) — physically it is a smaller proprietary Sennheiser shell, not a full-size XLR3. No bandwidth grade applies (analog mic-level audio). Other specs corroborated via B&H product listing and Sennheiser documentation: sensitivity 4 mV/Pa, max SPL 150 dB, impedance 1 kΩ nominal, weight 9.2 g (capsule) / 455 g (as shipped w/ full assembly), frequency response 40 Hz–20 kHz.
